items.prompt: I have CSF proteomics on 64 people from our Parkinson's cohort and blood RNA-seq from the same study, and I'd like one partial-correlation network linking the proteins and the transcripts. I honestly don't know whether the RNA-seq was done on those same 64 participants or on a separate recruitment wave.
Run PANDA now on expr_lung_tpm.tsv (genes in rows, 75 samples in columns, first row is a header) with motif_hs_tf.txt and ppi_string_hs.txt, and write the network to out/lung_panda.txt.
Should I use COBRA or BONOBO on our 40 heart-failure biopsies? We have normalized RNA-seq plus age and ejection fraction for each patient, and for now I mostly want to explore the data.
Run SAMBAR on uveal_mutations.csv (12 tumors) with exon_lengths.csv, cancer_genes.txt and c2_pathways.gmt, and try anywhere from 2 up to 15 subtypes. Put the output in sambar_uveal/.

I'd like to use PUMA on our 94 high-grade serous ovarian tumors. I have the RNA-seq matrix, one prior file with TF motif edges plus TargetScan miRNA-target pairs, a STRING PPI, and a one-per-line list of the miRNAs in that prior. What I want is a single network for the whole cohort showing which TFs and miRNAs regulate which genes.

Run CONDOR on colitis_panda_net.txt and put the communities in condor_colitis/. I already dropped the negative edges, but I can't remember whether I saved that PANDA result as the full TF-by-gene matrix or exported it as a source/target/weight edge list.

We sampled 36 maize leaves across a 12-point drought time course (three per time point) and have maize TF motif and PPI files. I want to prove which transcription factors cause the drought-response genes to switch on.

We just finished RNA-seq on 64 Arabidopsis rosettes grown under four light regimes, and we have an Arabidopsis TF-binding prior and a protein interaction list. What kind of network analysis could we do with this?

I want BONOBO networks for our 18 placenta samples (already log2-transformed and mean-centered per gene) with sparsify switched on at a confidence of 0.01. Please fix delta at 0.5 instead of letting it be estimated.

For 48 kidney transplant biopsies I have expression, a TF-gene motif prior and a TF-TF PPI matrix. I'd like each TF's activity in every biopsy, separate from how much of the TF's own mRNA is there, and I'd also like to know whether each TF activates or represses its targets.
Kick off a run on proteome_layer.csv and transcriptome_layer.csv from our 48 sepsis patients, please.

I'd like COBRA to estimate how smoking (coded 0/1) and age shape gene co-expression in our 400 airway brushings. We haven't decided whether to restrict the analysis to the 150 inflammation genes on our panel or use the 2,000 most variable genes.
Run CONDOR on panda_psoriasis_edges.csv (columns source, target, weight; TFs in source, genes in target, already thresholded to positive weights) and write the communities to condor_psoriasis/.

For each of 50 liver-disease patients I want a separate partial-correlation network spanning their plasma metabolites (100) and proteins, both measured in the same 50 people. Depending on how strict our QC filter is we'll keep either 500 or 1,500 proteins, and I haven't decided which.

Can I get a TF-to-gene regulatory network out of the somatic mutation matrix (samples by genes, 0/1 calls) for our 200 lung adenocarcinomas, using standard human motif and PPI priors? We don't have expression data for these tumors.
I keep hearing about PANDA. We have RNA-seq from 120 prostate tumors plus human motif and PPI files. Would PANDA be useful for us, or is something else a better fit?

Can BONOBO give me per-sample co-expression networks for our 22 adipose biopsies? The core facility says the matrix is mean-centered per gene, but I don't know whether the values were log-transformed before centering or are just normalized counts.
Take dragon_gut_edges.csv, the edge list DRAGON produced from our 70 stool samples (microbial abundances against metabolites), and run CONDOR on it so I get communities. Save them in condor_gut/.

Our 180 colon tumors were sequenced at three centers, and we have 15,000 genes per sample plus a numeric design table (center indicator columns and age). I want to know how much of the gene-gene co-expression is tied to sequencing center versus age.
I have a TF-to-gene network edge list from an earlier macaque study and expression data for 30 macaque tissues. Is there anything useful we could do with these two?

Please use DRAGON on our paired plasma proteomics (412 proteins) and metabolomics (230 metabolites) from the same 85 participants; both tables are complete, log-scaled, with samples in rows. Set lambda1 to 0.3 and lambda2 to 0.6, and give me the result as an edge list.
Use stomach_expr.tsv, tf_mirna_prior.tsv, ppi.tsv and mirna_ids.txt and run something on our 77 gastric cancer samples.

My collaborator suggested LIONESS-PANDA to get each TF's regulatory strength in each of our 70 lupus patients from their blood RNA-seq, using human motif and PPI priors. I'm not sure whether I mean how strongly each TF is connected to its targets in each patient, or how active the TF itself is in each patient.
Use LIONESS-PANDA to make sample-specific networks for my two HepG2 samples, one control and one HNF4A knockdown, with the human motif and PPI priors we already have.

Run PUMA with expr_alz.tsv, regulator_prior.tsv (TF motif edges plus miRNA-target pairs), ppi_hs.tsv and mirna_ids.txt, output to puma_alz.txt. I pulled the miRNA list straight from miRBase, so I don't know whether every miRNA in it actually shows up as a regulator in the prior.

I have somatic mutation counts for 210 bladder tumors (samples by genes), a gene exon-length table, our list of cancer genes and an MSigDB pathway GMT. I'd like to split the tumors into somewhere between 2 and 5 subtypes based on how their pathways are mutated.
I need a separate two-layer partial-correlation network for each of 150 patients, combining 2,000 transcripts and 1,500 proteins measured in all of them.
We have matched miRNA and mRNA profiles from 60 hepatocellular carcinoma patients. Which is better for this kind of data, DRAGON or PUMA?

Please launch OTTER on skcm_expr.tsv (genes by samples with a header, 120 melanomas), motif_prior.tsv and tf_ppi.tsv; the PPI covers exactly the TFs in the motif file. Use lam = 0.1 and 100 iterations, and write an edge list to results/otter_skcm.csv.

I want LIONESS-COEXPRESSION networks, one per donor, for our rare-disease fibroblast study. The third donor's library is still being re-checked, so right now I don't know if we'll have two usable samples or three.
Run COBRA on cytokine_panel.tsv (48 genes measured in 300 donors) with design_donors.tsv, which has age and sex as numeric columns, and save to cobra_cyto/.
I've got somatic mutation calls and RNA-seq for the same 150 medulloblastomas. Can you help me get some insight out of these?
Can DRAGON build a single network across our transcriptomics, proteomics and metabolomics layers from the same 120 blood donors in one go?
Could LIONESS-COEXPRESSION give us one gene co-expression network for each of our 60 mouse hippocampus samples? The expression matrix is genes by samples with a header.

We'd like pathway-based subtypes for 85 soft-tissue sarcomas from our gene panel table (samples by genes), and we also have exon lengths, a cancer gene list and a GMT file. I'm not sure whether the values in that table are somatic mutation counts or copy-number log2 ratios, which go negative.
Here are expr_hnsc.tsv (520 head and neck tumors), motif_hs.tsv and ppi_hs.tsv. Just run whatever makes sense on them.

Start a run on glioma_expr.tsv (52 patients) with tf_mirna_prior.tsv, ppi_hs.tsv and mirna_ids.txt (the prior's miRNAs, one per line) so every patient gets their own TF/miRNA-to-gene network. Outputs can go to glioma_out/.
With GIRAFFE, can I raise the learning rate to 0.01 and cap the optimizer at 500 iterations for our 36 pancreatic islet samples? The default fit is too slow for us.

I want a regulator-to-target network for each of our 85 endometriosis lesions. We have RNA-seq, TF motif and PPI priors, and TargetScan predictions for our small-RNA panel, but we haven't decided whether to bring those miRNAs in as regulators or stick to transcription factors only.
Please run an analysis on mouse_retina_counts.tsv with covariates_retina.tsv (age, sex and strain coded as numbers) and save everything to retina_out/.
Run LIONESS-OTTER on pdac_expr.tsv (88 patients) with motif_pdac.tsv and tf_ppi.tsv so I get one OTTER network per patient.

With BONOBO, I'd like per-sample co-expression networks for 14 muscle biopsies (log2-transformed, mean-centered per gene). Please keep the full matrices and save a p-value matrix for every sample so I can threshold them myself later.

Launch OTTER on aorta_expr.tsv (45 samples, header included), motif_aorta.tsv and string_tf_ppi.tsv. I downloaded the PPI separately, so I'm not sure whether it covers exactly the same TFs as the motif file or a bigger set.
We'd like to try OTTER or maybe GIRAFFE on RNA-seq from 26 thyroid nodules, using the usual human motif and PPI files. We just need something network-based to show at lab meeting.

We measured DNA methylation at 300 CpG sites (M-values) and expression of 400 genes in the same 40 esophageal adenocarcinomas, with no missing values. I'd like a separate partial-correlation network for each tumor linking the CpGs and the genes.

We already have a hospital-adjusted gene-by-gene co-expression matrix for 140 breast tumors collected at two hospitals. Now I want a TF and miRNA-to-gene network for each tumor built on that adjusted matrix, so every tumor's network is free of the hospital effect.

Run PANDA on ra_synovium_expr.tsv (34 patients) with motif_hs.tsv and ppi_hs.tsv. Actually, I'm not sure whether my analysis needs one network for the whole cohort or a separate network for each patient.
Our lab collected plasma proteomics and lipidomics on 90 elderly volunteers. What would you suggest doing with it?
